questions.q: What kind of checks do heuristic quality filters typically use?
options: A full trained neural network for every document
Simple, fast rules like document length bounds, alphabetic-character ratio, and stop-word ratio
Manual human review of every single document
Only checking whether the document contains images
questions.explain: Heuristic filters use cheap, rule-based checks -- length bounds, character-type ratios, stop-word presence -- to catch obviously broken documents before any model-based filtering runs.

questions.q: What does perplexity-based filtering with a tool like KenLM measure?
options: The exact number of unique words in a document
How 'surprised' a small language model trained on known high-quality text is by a candidate document
The toxicity level of the text
The number of personally identifiable details in the text
questions.explain: KenLM-style perplexity filtering trains a lightweight n-gram model on high-quality reference text, then scores documents by how statistically unexpected (high perplexity) they are under that model -- flagging likely gibberish or corrupted text.

questions.q: Why might a pipeline use a fastText classifier instead of a larger neural network for quality classification?
options: fastText classifiers are more accurate than any other method in all cases
fastText is a lightweight, fast linear classifier well suited to scoring documents at web scale
fastText cannot be used for text classification at all
fastText eliminates the need for any heuristic filtering
questions.explain: fastText's speed as a lightweight linear classifier makes it practical to run over web-scale corpora, where a slower, larger model would be prohibitively expensive to apply to every document.

questions.q: What is the role of tools like Perspective API or Detoxify in this pipeline?
options: They measure how grammatically correct a document is
They score text for toxicity-related categories like hate speech and harassment, independent of quality scoring
They tokenize text into subword units
They deduplicate near-identical documents
questions.explain: Perspective API and Detoxify output per-category probability scores (toxicity, harassment, identity attack, etc.) used to filter harmful content, which is a distinct concern from whether text is well-formed prose.

questions.q: Why is PII scrubbing treated as a separate pass from quality and toxicity filtering?
options: PII scrubbing is actually identical to toxicity filtering
Well-written, non-toxic text can still contain personally identifiable information like emails or phone numbers that shouldn't be memorized by the model
PII scrubbing only applies to code datasets, never to web text
PII scrubbing replaces the need for deduplication
questions.explain: A document can be high-quality and non-toxic while still containing emails, phone numbers, or ID numbers. PII scrubbing uses pattern matching and named-entity recognition as its own independent pass to catch this regardless of quality or toxicity scores.
